exposure: Rhesus (Rh) alloimmunization treated with intrauterine blood transfusion (IUT)
cohort: The study included 144 neonates delivered between January 2015 and December 2021, comprising 72 with Rhesus hemolytic disease (RHD) who received intrauterine blood transfusion (IUT) and 72 control neonates without Rh-isoimmunization or IUT.
finding: Neonates with Rhesus hemolytic disease (RHD) who underwent intrauterine blood transfusion (IUT) were at a higher risk of developing Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) and required a prolonged course of respiratory support.
